program_name: Master in Eco-Social Design. The name is NOT translated by unibz in any language version: the English, German, Italian and Ladin navigation all read 'Master in Eco-Social Design', and the Italian programme page does not exist as a translation at all — https://www.unibz.it/it/faculties/design-art/master-eco-social-design returns the notice 'Siamo spiacenti, questa pagina non è disponibile in italiano. Vai alla pagina in inglese.' (Sorry, this page is not available in Italian. Go to the English page.). The English page itself carries the banner 'This page is only available in English'. This is a meaningful signal: unlike almost every other unibz programme, Eco-Social Design is presented monolingually in English even at the marketing level. Delivered by the FACULTY OF DESIGN AND ART (Fakultät für Design und Künste / Facoltà di Design e Arti), which also runs the Bachelor in Design and Art (Majors in Design and in Art), the Master in Critical Creative Practices, the PhD in Experimental Research through Design, Art and Technologies, and the 1st Level Master in Future of Art Museums (FOAM). unibz's own shorthand in the brochure career section is 'MA Eco-Social Design'; some third-party aggregators mislabel it 'Master of Science in Eco-Social Design', which is wrong — the Italian award is a laurea magistrale in class LM-12 and the faculty consistently uses 'MA'. PEOPLE (from the programme page): 'Degree course director: Prof. Secil Ugur Yavuz'; 'Student Representative in the Course Council: Marieke Kathrin Schäfer'. The programme runs its own public-facing platform, the blog 'BY DESIGN AND BY DISASTER' at https://designdisaster.unibz.it/, and a self-produced introductory presentation PDF hosted on Google Drive (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1FKbzky0_3miTS9C5T3eOpkBjXAxdDmps/view?usp=sharing), both linked from the official page: 'Additionally, to this web page, you can get more insights by this presentation (PDF) and on our blog.' Student output is published in the Faculty's 'Showcase and Projects Archive', which covers 'the works created by our students since 2018 in the two Majors in Design, the Major in Art and the Master in Eco-Social Design'. AlmaLaurea transparency code (CODICIONE) for this programme: 0210107301300001.
level: Master (Italian 'laurea magistrale', second-cycle degree, EQF/NQF level 7). Brochure 'At a glance', verbatim: 'Degree class: LM-12 / ECTS credits: 120 / Duration of the course: 2 years'. Four semesters, 120 ECTS, taught entirely in English on the Bozen-Bolzano campus. The award is a Master of Arts (the faculty writes 'MA Eco-Social Design'), NOT an MSc, despite some third-party listings claiming otherwise. ENTRY QUALIFICATION is a bachelor degree; at enrolment the Diploma Supplement must show 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS)' and 'that the qualification gives access to a Master programme'. CREDIT ARCHITECTURE (from the published study plan): 45 CP of studio projects (Project 1 = 15 CP, Project 2 = 15 CP, Thesis Project Phase 1 = 15 CP), 18 CP in the 'Make and Intervene' area, 18 CP in the 'Observe, Analyse and Apply' area, 3 CP 'English 1 – Language Course', 12 CP Free Choice Courses, 6 CP Seminars, 18 CP Degree Thesis. Total 120 CP. In addition, zero-credit but COMPULSORY technical workshop courses: 'Workshop courses do not carry credits, but attendance is mandatory', preceded by 'the mandatory safety training (Work Safety – Machinery Hazard – Chemical Risk)'. PROGRESSION: the degree gives access to doctoral study; unibz itself runs a directly related doctorate, the PhD in Experimental Research through Design, Art and Technologies, in the same faculty. NO Italian state professional qualification (esame di Stato) is attached to LM-12 in the way LM-73 leads to the agronomist/forester register — nothing in the 2026/27 documents claims a professional-register pathway. GRADE OUTCOMES (unibz's published 'Grade Statistics LM-12' page): individual exams are graded 18–30 with a distribution heavily skewed high — 30 = 22.91%, 28 = 21.61%, 29 = 17.29%, 27 = 15.13%, 30 cum laude = 8.21%, 26 = 6.20%, 25 = 4.32%, 24 = 2.16%, 23 = 0.72%, 20 = 1.01%, 22 = 0.14%, 18 = 0.29%. Final graduation grades (out of 110): 110 = 44.23%, 110 cum laude = 15.38%, 108 = 7.69%, 107 = 7.69%, 106 = 7.69%, 104 = 3.85%, 109 = 3.85%, and 96 / 99 / 102 / 103 / 105 at 1.92% each. Nearly 60% of graduates finish at 110 or 110 cum laude, i.e. the programme is hard to get INTO and comparatively generous once inside.
teaching_language: FULLY AND EXCLUSIVELY ENGLISH — this is NOT one of unibz's trilingual programmes, and it is more monolingual than most of unibz's other 'English-taught' masters. Brochure 'At a glance', verbatim: 'Courses will be taught in: English'. Admission-information PDF, verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English.' VERIFIED AT COURSE LEVEL, not just at marketing level: the official course-offering page for the cohort 'enrolled after 2025' lists every single course with language tag EN — Design & Materials, Information Design & Visual Storytelling, Political Ecology, Eco-social Economics, Moderation & Participation, Design & Production, Media Studies, Social Studies of Design and Culture, Environmental Anthropology, Service and Policy Design, Emancipatory Digital Transformation, Project 1, Project 2, the Thesis Project Phase 1 variants and all seminars. No course is offered in Italian or German. The only admission language requirement is English B2. There is NO German and NO Italian requirement at entry. The application itself, the project proposal, the portfolio, the CV and the interview are all in English: 'curriculum vitae in English (pdf)'; 'The required language is English'; 'portfolio in English (pdf)'. ONE INTERNAL LANGUAGE ELEMENT: the study plan contains a compulsory 3 CP course 'English 1 – Language Course' delivered by the unibz Language Centre — i.e. English is not only the medium but also a small assessed component of the degree. CONTRAST WITH SISTER PROGRAMMES: the Bachelor in Design and Art in the same faculty is trilingual (IT/DE/EN) and therefore effectively closed to English-only applicants; Eco-Social Design is the faculty's fully English route. PRACTICAL NUANCE, not a formal requirement: Bozen-Bolzano is an officially bilingual German/Italian city and the programme's projects are deliberately grounded in the local territory — 'you do a project starting off from a given local and provincial context', with 'external partners you choose' (NGOs, cooperatives, craft businesses, public bodies). Fieldwork, co-design sessions and stakeholder interviews in South Tyrol will frequently involve German- or Italian-speaking partners even though all teaching, supervision and assessment are in English. German or Italian is therefore useful for project quality and for daily life, but is never required to be admitted or to graduate.
campus: BOZEN-BOLZANO MAIN CAMPUS ONLY — a single-site, single-country programme. Brochure 'At a glance': 'Campus: Bozen-Bolzano'. Address: Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Italy. NOT at NOI Techpark Bolzano, NOT at Brixen-Bressanone, NOT at Bruneck-Brunico, and unlike EMMA (Bolzano + Innsbruck) or the Master in Energy Engineering (Bolzano + Trento) there is NO second-university or second-country year. Everything — all four semesters, the thesis and the defence — happens in Bozen-Bolzano. THE PHYSICAL SETUP IS THE PROGRAMME'S DEFINING ASSET and is described at length by unibz: 'The spacious and sunny ateliers are open spaces for creative development and collaboration. Here you work in teams on your projects, in constant exchange with other students and the teachers.' WORKSHOPS, verbatim: 'Our superbly equipped workshops offer a wide range of technologies for your design work, such as workshops for wood, metal, plastic, materials, digital modelling, plaster and mold making, surface treatment, printing (screen, tampon and high pressure), paper and bookbinding, photography, video and access to the Fab Lab BITZ.' Workshop access is gated: 'To attend them, you must first complete the mandatory safety training (Work Safety – Machinery Hazard – Chemical Risk), as required by current regulations. In the first semester, you will attend introductory workshop courses, which are compulsory to access the specialised ones. From the second semester onwards, you must choose and attend at least one specialised workshop.' ATTENDANCE: the 2026/27 documents state no general compulsory-attendance rule for lectures, but workshop attendance IS mandatory ('Workshop courses do not carry credits, but attendance is mandatory') and seminar attendance is mandatory ('Attendance of the seminars is compulsory and foresees a pass/fail test'). Because the degree is built on studio projects with external partners, it is in practice a full-time, physically present programme — there is no distance or part-time variant. MOBILITY: 'Currently we offer exchange programmes with partner universities all over the world and we are part of a large network of collaboration with employers in Italy and abroad where you can undertake your internship. However, this study programme does not require a compulsory internship.'
degree_class: LM-12 — 'Design', the Italian ministerial second-cycle degree class for design. Stated verbatim in the brochure 'At a glance' ('Degree class: LM-12'), on the programme page, and reflected in the title of unibz's own statistics page for this programme, 'Grade Statistics LM-12'. It is the natural second cycle above the Italian bachelor class L-4 (Disegno industriale), which is exactly why L-4 heads the list of directly qualifying entry classes. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE — the double-enrolment rule, verbatim from the admission-information PDF: 'According to national regulations, simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is possible (however, the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., LM-69/LM-69 and must differ for at least 2/3 of the course contents).' [uncertain] TWO BOILERPLATE ERRORS TO IGNORE: that sentence cites 'LM-69/LM-69' (LM-69 is Agricultural Science and Technology, nothing to do with design), and the signed 2026/27 ranking list uses a different wrong example, 'e.g., LM-18/LM-18' (LM-18 is Computer Science). Both are copy-paste artefacts from other unibz programmes' templates. The rule an Eco-Social Design applicant must actually apply is LM-12/LM-12: you may not hold simultaneous enrolment in a second LM-12 design master, and any second programme must differ in at least two-thirds of its content. Neither document ever states the correct example for this programme. A THIRD DOCUMENTED SHIFT: the archived 2022/23 admission PDF said the opposite — 'Concurrent enrolment at several universities or in several study programmes at the same university is not allowed.' Italian law changed (L. 33/2022) and unibz updated the clause; the 2026/27 permissive rule is the current one. LM-12 also governs which Italian bachelor classes are treated as directly qualifying and shapes the 10-ECTS design-sector threshold used for everyone else (see academic_requirements).
