is_new_programme: NOT a new programme — Eco-Social Design is a mature, internationally visible master with roughly eleven completed intakes. FOUNDED: the programme started with the academic year 2015/16, after a preparation phase whose public milestone was the first 'By Design or by Disaster' conference in 2013. The programme's own blog marked the anniversary with a post titled '10 years of Eco-Social Design* and now?' (designdisaster.unibz.it). [uncertain] The 2015/16 start date comes from the programme's own blog and third-party listings rather than from a dated unibz administrative document; unibz does not publish a founding year in the brochure or admission PDF. EVIDENCE OF MATURITY: (a) unibz publishes a full 'Grade Statistics LM-12' page including a distribution of FINAL GRADUATION grades — which only exists once many cohorts have graduated — with 44.23% of graduates at 110 and 15.38% at 110 cum laude; (b) a named Student Representative sits on the Course Council (Marieke Kathrin Schäfer); (c) unibz links AlmaLaurea graduate-satisfaction and employability statistics (CODICIONE 0210107301300001); (d) the Faculty's Showcase and Projects Archive has published student work 'since 2018'; (e) the programme sustains its own conference series and blog. DOCUMENTED EVOLUTION 2022/23 → 2026/27 (comparing the archived 2022/23 admission PDF with the current one). The admission MECHANICS are remarkably stable — the same two-stage structure, the same 20+20 stage-1 split, the same 20-point interview, the same 20/40 gate and the same 30/60 pass mark existed already in 2022/23. What changed: (i) PLACES were rebalanced from 17 EU Early Bird + 8 EU Late + 9 non-EU (2022/23) to 15 + 10 + 10 (2026/27) — the non-EU allocation grew and the Late session grew at the Early Bird session's expense; (ii) the EXIT LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT disappeared — 2022/23 stated 'Exit level (to graduate) English: C1'; the 2026/27 document has no exit level at all (see exit_levels); (iii) the ACCADEMIE DI BELLE ARTI / ISIA route was removed from the printed entry list — 2022/23 explicitly admitted holders of a 'Diploma Accademico di primo livello' (DAPL03, DAPL04, DAPL05, DAPL06, DAPL08, DIPL01, DIPL02); the 2026/27 list no longer names them; (iv) the APPLICATION FEE for non-EU applicants rose from € 30 to € 50; (v) the PORTFOLIO FORMAT tightened — 2022/23 allowed 'conversion of a web-based portfolio (e.g. Behance) in PDF format indicating the URL'; 2026/27 demands 'a fully illustrated and written portfolio as a PDF only' with a 20 MB cap and warns the commission 'reserves the right to decline a portfolio that is not readily accessible to them'; (vi) the MINIMUM-ENROLMENT clause ('a minimum of 12 newly enrolled students') was dropped; (vii) the SIMULTANEOUS-ENROLMENT ban was replaced by the permissive two-programme rule; (viii) the STUDY PLAN was revised for the 2025 intake — unibz maintains two separate course offerings, 'Course Offering - enrolled after 2025' and 'Course offering - enrolled before 2025'. NET READING: an old, stable, well-documented programme that has been progressively formalised and slightly internationalised, not an experimental new launch.
majors_tracks_study_plans: ONE SINGLE STUDY PLAN — no majors, no tracks, no curricula, no separate admission codes and no separate quotas. This distinguishes it from the sister Bachelor in Design and Art, which splits into a Major in Design and a Major in Art with separate admission. Everyone applying to Eco-Social Design applies to the same thing. PERSONALISATION IS BUILT IN THROUGH CHOICE, NOT THROUGH TRACKS: 'You have the possibility to set your personal focus, by choosing what to deepen within the rich set of design disciplines and sciences offered in the study program.' unibz describes the two supervision lines available for project work as 'object-space-services and communication-interaction-services' — these are supervision emphases, not formal tracks. THE ONE FORMAL BINARY CHOICE is inside the third-semester thesis preparation. Study plan, verbatim: '15 CP Thesis Project Phase 1: Research through Design, Exploration and Experimentation (A)* — 9 CP Design 3 + 6 CP Sociological Design Research' versus '15 CP Thesis Project Phase 1: Research through Design, Exploration and Experimentation (B)* — 9 CP Design 3 + 6 CP Designing through ethnography', with the footnote '* Thesis Project Phase 1: Students have to choose 1 Thesis Project Phase among (A) or (B).' So the only structural fork in the whole degree is sociological design research versus design ethnography. FULL STUDY PLAN (120 CP). PROJECTS, 45 CP: 'Project 1 in Eco-Social Design' 15 CP (12 CP Design 1 + 3 CP Design Research related to project 1); 'Project 2 in Eco-Social Design' 15 CP (12 CP Design 2 + 3 CP Design Research related to project 2); Thesis Project Phase 1 (A) or (B) 15 CP. AREA 'MAKE AND INTERVENE', 18 CP: 'Emancipatory Digital Transformation' 6 CP (fully mandatory); then '1 Mandatory Course to be chosen among the following: Moderation and Participation / Service and Policy Design' 6 CP; then '1 Mandatory Course to be chosen among the following: Design and Production / Design and Materials / Information Design and Visual Storytelling' 6 CP. AREA 'OBSERVE, ANALYSE AND APPLY', 18 CP: '3 Mandatory Courses to be chosen among the following: Media Studies / Social Studies of Design and Culture / Ecosocial Economics / Political Ecology / Environmental Anthropology', 6 CP each. PLUS: 'English 1 – Language Course' 3 CP; 'Free Choice Courses' 12 CP; 'Seminars' 6 CP; 'Degree Thesis' 18 CP. FREE CHOICE, verbatim: 'Students have to choose free choice courses for a total amount of 12 credit points. These courses may be chosen among those offered by the Faculty of Design and Art and/or those of the other faculties of unibz. At the beginning of each academic year, the Faculty announces which courses are offered and recognised as free choice.' The programme page adds: 'If you want to extend your study plan further, you can choose courses from other faculties.' SEMINARS, verbatim: 'During the 4 semesters, students must attend 3 seminars which provide useful knowledge for the introduction in to the job market, among the offered ones, for a total of 6 credits. Attendance of the seminars is compulsory and foresees a pass/fail test.' Named seminars: 'Cooperatives (funding and running a democratic and socio-ecological business)', 'Transformative Work as a Livelihood', 'Project Funding for Eco-Social Designers'; the course-offering page also lists 'Seminar 3: Learning from Experts'. SEMESTER RHYTHM: semester 1 — a guided project 'starting off from a given local and provincial context'; semester 2 — 'an autonomous project, in teams or individually, together with external partners you choose'; semester 3 — 'research through design and creative experimentation on a topic of your choice', accompanied by the 'Master Colloquia'; semester 4 — 'your final project including a comprehensive written thesis', supervised by a supervisor and co-supervisor and defended before a commission. ZERO-CREDIT COMPULSORY LAYER: technical workshop courses (see campus). TWO COHORT VERSIONS OF THE PLAN: unibz publishes 'Course Offering - enrolled after 2025' and 'Course offering - enrolled before 2025' as separate pages, so the plan was revised for the 2025 intake. [uncertain] unibz does not publish a changelog explaining what differs between the pre-2025 and post-2025 plans. NO OTHER VARIANTS: no dual-study or apprenticeship model, no part-time route, no double degree with a partner university, and 'this study programme does not require a compulsory internship'.
english_only_accessibility: OPEN — one of the most genuinely accessible programmes at unibz for an applicant who speaks only English, with one large caveat that is about EVIDENCE, not about ability. WHY IT IS OPEN: (a) the sole language requirement is English B2 — 'Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2'; (b) there is NO German and NO Italian requirement at entry, NO third-language B1 threshold, and no exit language level stated in the 2026/27 documents; (c) every course in the published course offering is tagged EN, so an English-only student can complete 120 CP without encountering a German or Italian course — unlike EMMA, where the second-year elective menu at Innsbruck includes German options; (d) the entire application — CV, project proposal, portfolio, interview — is in English; (e) the campus is a single site in Bozen-Bolzano with no relocation to a second country; (f) the sister Bachelor in Design and Art in the same faculty is trilingual and effectively closed to English-only candidates, which makes Eco-Social Design the faculty's designated international route. THE CAVEAT — THE LANGUAGE GATE IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST DOCUMENTED KILLER IN THIS PROGRAMME'S ADMISSION, and it kills people who almost certainly speak English well enough. In the signed 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list, NINE EU/parity applicants (IDs 150498, 149844, 140507, 145298, 153713, 154365, 155633, 155035, 156074) were listed under: 'The following persons do not meet the language requirements for admission and are therefore excluded from the admission procedure. They may re-apply in the second session.' That is 9 out of the roughly 40 EU applicants documented in that list — about 22%, and far higher than the ~5% seen in EMMA. The non-EU list adds that unranked applicants 'were excluded from the admission procedure because they did not meet the admission requirements (language and/or study title)'. In a competition for 15 places, nine people were removed before their portfolio was even scored. The lesson is blunt: for a design applicant the temptation is to pour everything into the portfolio and treat the language paperwork as an afterthought; at unibz that is the most common way to lose. PROOF THAT IT IS RECOVERABLE: applicant ID 140507 was language-excluded in the Early Bird round and then admitted at rank 5 with a score of 39 in the Late round. The exclusion is an evidence failure, not a verdict on the candidate. PRACTICAL SOFT FACTORS: Bozen-Bolzano is officially bilingual German/Italian, and the programme deliberately grounds semester-1 work in 'a given local and provincial context' with local external partners. Fieldwork, co-design workshops and stakeholder conversations will often involve German- or Italian-speaking people. This affects the RICHNESS of what an English-only student can do in local projects, not their ability to pass anything. unibz Language Centre courses are available voluntarily. FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT specifically: a background in Endüstriyel Tasarım, Grafik Tasarım, İç Mimarlık, Mimarlık, Peyzaj Mimarlığı, Şehir ve Bölge Planlama, Görsel İletişim Tasarımı or Fotoğraf/Sinema-TV will normally clear the 10-ECTS design-sector threshold easily, and an English-medium bachelor is recognised outright as C1 with no test. The three things that actually decide the outcome are: getting the language evidence right the first time, the portfolio, and the two-page project proposal.
admission_type: RESTRICTED ACCESS (numero programmato), decided by a TWO-STAGE, PORTFOLIO-AND-INTERVIEW selection. This is a creative-practice admission, not an academic-record admission — and that is the single most important structural fact about it. NOT USED: no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GRE, no GMAT, no unibz written entrance exam, no motivation letter, no reference letters, no video presentation, no Excel study-career template, and — remarkably — no scoring of the bachelor grade at all. USED: a portfolio, a two-page illustrated project proposal, a CV, and an online interview. THE PROCEDURE, verbatim from the admission-information PDF: 'The admission procedure includes two stages. Stage 1: Evaluation of the documents. The first step is an evaluation of the documents that must be uploaded by the respective application deadline. Selection criteria of stage 1: Portfolio: max 20 points; outline of a project proposal: max 20 points. In order to be eligible for the second stage, you must have obtained at least 20 points.' Then: 'Stage 2: Interview. Max. 20 points. The second stage consists in an online interview designed to have a dialogue to get a deeper understanding on the candidate's ideas, experiences, motivations and points of view.' And: 'Candidates must achieve a minimum score of 30/60 total points to be eligible for the enrolment.' The signed ranking list restates the same structure and adds the gate wording used in the published exclusion tables: applicants 'were not eligible to the second stage of the admission procedure as they did not reach 20/40 points'. SO THERE ARE THREE SEQUENTIAL FILTERS: (1) an ELIGIBILITY CHECK on the entry qualification (Italian degree class or 10 design-sector ECTS, or a committee assessment of a foreign career) AND on English B2 — failing either removes you before scoring; (2) a STAGE-1 GATE at 20/40 on portfolio + project proposal; (3) a FINAL THRESHOLD of 30/60 after the interview, below which you are excluded even if places remain (this actually happened in 2026/27: non-EU applicant 154552 scored 28 and was excluded although the non-EU quota of 10 was not filled). TIE-BREAK, verbatim: 'In the event of equal total points, priority shall be given in the following order: score obtained for the draft project proposal; score obtained for the interview; score obtained for the portfolio. Only in case of equal scores, the youngest candidate will be chosen.' Note the ordering: the PROJECT PROPOSAL outranks the portfolio in a tie — the two-page document a candidate writes for this application is treated as more diagnostic than years of accumulated work. Applications go through the unibz Application Portal at https://aws.unibz.it/exup. 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified.' 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.' STABILITY: this exact procedure — same stages, same 20/20/20 split, same 20/40 gate, same 30/60 pass mark, same tie-break order — is already present in the archived 2022/23 admission PDF. It is one of the most stable admission procedures at unibz and is unlikely to change for 2027/28.
academic_requirements:
THREE ROUTES, AND THE THIRD IS DELIBERATELY WIDE. Admission-information PDF and signed ranking list, verbatim: 'In order to gain admission to this programme you need a bachelor degree in one of the following Italian degree classes: M.D. 270/04: L-4 Disegno industriale; L-17 Scienze dell’Architettura; L-21 Scienze della pianificazione territoriale, urbanistica, paesaggistica e ambientale. M.D. 509/99: 42 Disegno industriale; 04 Scienze dell’architettura e dell’ingegneria edile; 07 Urbanistica e scienza della pianificazione territoriale, urbanistica, paesaggistica e ambientale. If you have another Italian degree, you need 10 credit points in the following scientific disciplinary sectors: ICAR/13 Industrial Design; ICAR/14 Architectural and Urban Composition; ICAR/15 Landscape Design; ICAR/16 Interior and Decorative Architecture; ICAR/17 Representation of Architecture; ICAR/21 Urban design and landscape; L-ART/06 Cinema, photography and television; ING-INF/05 Information processing systems; INF-01 Informatics. If you have a degree from the Italian old system (prior to D.M. 509/99), or a title from another degree, or a degree obtained abroad, the selection committee will examine your career to determine your eligibility for admission.' 

ROUTE 1 — direct Italian classes L-4 / L-17 / L-21 (or the 509/99 equivalents 42 / 04 / 07). ROUTE 2 — any other Italian degree plus just 10 ECTS in the listed design/architecture/planning/media/informatics sectors. TEN credits is an extraordinarily low bar by unibz standards: the Master in Energy Engineering demands 85 ECTS across three blocks and EMMA demands 50. Ten ECTS is one or two courses. This is a deliberate design choice — the programme wants activists, anthropologists, engineers and economists who have touched design, and it filters them on portfolio rather than on transcript. ROUTE 3 — FOREIGN DEGREES ARE HANDLED BY HUMAN JUDGEMENT, not by a credit table: 'the selection committee will examine your career to determine your eligibility for admission.' There is no published ECTS threshold, no published mapping of foreign subjects onto Italian SSD codes, and no self-service way to verify eligibility. An older wording, from the archived 2022/23 PDF, gives the most useful plain-English gloss of what the committee is looking for and is worth reading: a degree of another class 'can be valued as adequate if, during your study career and before the beginning of the admission procedure, you have gained 10 credit points in the following fields: Design, Architecture and Spatial Planning, Landscape architecture, Interior Design, Cinema, Photography or Informatics. A commission checks the validity and equivalence of the credit points.' 

[uncertain] THE SSD LIST IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT AND PARTLY OBSOLETE. Eight of the nine codes are PRE-2024 codes (ICAR/13, ICAR/14, ICAR/15, ICAR/16, ICAR/17, ICAR/21, L-ART/06, ING-INF/05), while one — 'INF-01 Informatics' — is a POST-2024 reform code. unibz has evidently patched one entry without migrating the rest. Under the 2024 reform the old ICAR design and planning sectors map broadly onto the new CEAR-xx/x family (architecture, urbanism, drawing/representation) and ING-INF/05 maps to the new informatics/information-processing codes, but unibz publishes no crosswalk for this programme. An applicant whose Italian transcript carries only new-format codes should ask the Faculty Secretariat to confirm the correspondence in writing before applying. 

[uncertain] A ROUTE THAT DISAPPEARED FROM THE PRINTED LIST. The archived 2022/23 admission PDF explicitly admitted holders of an Italian 'Diploma Accademico di primo livello' from the Accademie di Belle Arti and the Istituti Superiori per le Industrie Artistiche, naming DAPL03 Scuola di decorazione, DAPL04 Scuola di grafica, DAPL05 Scuola di scenografia, DAPL06 Scuola di progettazione artistica per l’impresa, DAPL08 Scuola di nuove tecnologie dell’arte, DIPL01 Scuola di progettazione grafica ed editoriale and DIPL02 Scuola di Design. The 2026/27 documents no longer name them. Because AFAM first-level diplomas are legally equipollent to a bachelor degree in Italy, such candidates almost certainly still qualify through the catch-all committee route — but they are no longer guaranteed a place on the printed list and should confirm with the Faculty Secretariat. 

NOT YET GRADUATED: 'You can apply, but you will be admitted conditionally and need to submit your diploma by the enrolment deadline.' No minimum number of credits already earned is imposed — there is no '≥120 ECTS' rule as in some unibz masters. 

AT ENROLMENT the Diploma Supplement must state 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS)' and 'that the qualification gives access to a Master programme'. 

NO MINIMUM GRADE OF ANY KIND. There is no 22/30 floor, no GPA threshold, and no scoring of the bachelor grade. A candidate with a mediocre transcript and an outstanding portfolio is at no disadvantage whatsoever — this is the mirror image of EMMA, where the grade is the entire score. 

CREDIT RECOGNITION AFTER ENTRY: 'Credit points from previous university studies can only be recognised after enrolment if the exams taken at the university of provenance are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.' 

READING FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT: Endüstri Ürünleri Tasarımı, Grafik Tasarım, Görsel İletişim Tasarımı, İç Mimarlık ve Çevre Tasarımı, Mimarlık, Peyzaj Mimarlığı, Şehir ve Bölge Planlama, Sinema-TV and Fotoğraf programmes will comfortably exceed 10 ECTS in the listed fields. Less obvious but still viable: Sosyoloji, Antropoloji, İletişim, Çevre Mühendisliği or Bilgisayar Mühendisliği graduates who took design, visual communication, informatics or planning electives — the 10-credit bar is low and the committee route is discretionary. Because eligibility for a foreign degree is a human judgement, a Turkish applicant should e-mail design-art@unibz.it with an English transcript plus course descriptions well before the application window opens, and should prepare a 'declaration of value or similar document' stating the lowest passing grade and the highest obtainable grade.
entry_exam_or_test: NO WRITTEN OR STANDARDISED ENTRANCE EXAM OF ANY KIND. Specifically absent from all 2026/27 documents: no unibz admission test, no TOLC (TOLC-I, TOLC-E, TOLC-S), no CENT-S, no SAT, no GRE, no GMAT, no subject test, and no mathematics or logic test. Selection is made entirely from uploaded creative work plus an interview — see admission_type, selection_scoring and interview. THE ONLY EXAM AN APPLICANT MIGHT SIT is the ENGLISH LANGUAGE PROFICIENCY EXAM run by the unibz Language Centre, and only if they cannot prove B2 English by medium of instruction or by a recognised certificate. It is held ONLINE. 2026/27 sittings and registration windows, verbatim from the admission-information PDF: EARLY BIRD — 'Language exams (online): 16/03/2026 (registration: 02 - 09/03/2026) and 16 - 17 and 20 - 21/04/2026 (registration: 24/03 - 08/04/2026)'; LATE — 'Language exams (online): 22 - 26/06/2026 (registration: 28/05 - 15/06/2026)'. Note that this programme's Late window offers only ONE language-exam block (22–26/06/2026), whereas some other unibz programmes also list a July sitting — Eco-Social Design's Late application closes on 02/07/2026 and no July exam is offered for it. PROCEDURAL TRAP, verbatim: 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' Registration is a separate act from applying, it happens inside the Application Portal under 'enrol for language exams', and it only becomes available after an application has been created under 'create/manage applications'. Given that nine EU applicants were excluded on language in the 2026/27 Early Bird round, this sequencing is the most consequential piece of administrative fine print in the whole procedure. The one further assessed event in the admission process is the online INTERVIEW (14/05/2026 for Early Bird, 15/07/2026 for Late), which is a dialogue rather than an examination — see interview.
selection_scoring:
A 60-POINT RUBRIC IN WHICH THE BACHELOR GRADE COUNTS FOR NOTHING. This is the defining feature of the programme's admission and the opposite of every grade-driven unibz master. THE RUBRIC, verbatim: STAGE 1 — 'Portfolio: max 20 points; outline of a project proposal: max 20 points. In order to be eligible for the second stage, you must have obtained at least 20 points.' STAGE 2 — 'Interview: max 20 points.' OVERALL — 'Candidates must achieve a minimum score of 30/60 total points to be eligible for the enrolment.' TIE-BREAK, verbatim: 'In the event of equal total points, priority shall be given in the following order: score obtained for the draft project proposal; score obtained for the interview; score obtained for the portfolio. Only in case of equal scores, the youngest candidate will be chosen.' 

PUBLISHED 2026/27 RESULTS — unibz publishes INDIVIDUAL SCORES, so the competition can be measured precisely. 

EARLY BIRD, EU CITIZENS AND CITIZENS ENJOYING PARITY OF TREATMENT (15 places). Admitted, ranks 1–15 with scores: 58, 56, 55, 52, 51, 51, 50, 50, 49, 49, 49, 49, 48, 47, 44. Waiting list, ranks 16–24: 44, 42, 42, 39, 38, 35, 35, 33, 31. EFFECTIVE CUT-OFF: 44/60 — and note that the score 44 appears both at rank 15 (admitted) and rank 16 (waiting list), so the last place in the Early Bird round was decided purely by the tie-break, i.e. by the project-proposal sub-score. Excluded before the interview for failing the stage-1 gate ('did not reach 20/40 points'): 18, 17, 17, 15, 14, 14, 13 (7 applicants). Excluded on language: 9 applicants. Total EU applicants documented in that list: 40, competing for 15 places — a 37.5% documented admit rate, and unibz adds that further applicants 'not included in the ranking list were excluded from the admission procedure because they did not meet the admission requirements', so the true applicant pool was larger still. 

LATE APPLICATION, EU ONLY (10 places). Admitted, ranks 1–10: 55, 47, 46, 41, 39, 35, 35, 34, 33, 32. Waiting list, ranks 11–13: 30, 30, 30. One applicant excluded for not reaching the minimum: 25. Five excluded at the stage-1 gate: 17, 16, 15, 12, 10. EFFECTIVE CUT-OFF: 32/60. 

NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD, EARLY BIRD (10 places). Only NINE were admitted, with scores 55, 52, 48, 51, 42, 41, 37, 37, 32. One applicant scored 28 and was excluded: 'The following applicant did not reach the required minimum score of 30/60 and is therefore excluded from the ranking.' Fourteen more failed the stage-1 gate with 15, 14, 13, 12, 12, 11, 10, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2. EFFECTIVE CUT-OFF: 32/60 — but in reality the quota did NOT bind; the 30/60 absolute threshold did. unibz left a place empty rather than admit a candidate on 28. 

[uncertain] The published non-EU list is NOT in descending score order: rank 3 carries 48 and rank 4 carries 51. Either the ranks or the scores contain a transcription error in the signed PDF; unibz does not annotate it. Read the score column, not the rank column. 

THE MOST ACTIONABLE FINDING IN THE WHOLE DATASET — RE-APPLYING IN THE LATE SESSION WORKS. Three applicant IDs appear in both 2026/27 lists, and all three improved dramatically: ID 140507 was LANGUAGE-EXCLUDED in Early Bird and was then ADMITTED at rank 5 with 39 points in the Late round; ID 151897 scored 17/40 at the Early Bird stage-1 gate and was then ADMITTED at rank 8 with 34/60 in the Late round; ID 155407 scored 14/40 in Early Bird and reached the Late waiting list at rank 12 with 30/60. The admission PDF explicitly invites this: 'If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one.' 

STRATEGIC READING. (1) The Late session was FAR easier than Early Bird for EU applicants in 2026/27 — cut-off 32 versus 44, a 12-point gap on a 60-point scale. A borderline EU candidate is measurably better off in the Late round, which contradicts the usual 'apply early' advice. (2) The stage-1 gate is the real slaughter: 7 of 40 EU Early Bird applicants and 14 of 24 documented non-EU applicants never reached the interview. Non-EU scores at the gate were startlingly low — four applicants scored 4/40 and three scored 2–3/40, which suggests portfolios that simply did not address the brief. (3) Grades, university reputation, publications and work experience are worth ZERO points; the only currencies are portfolio, proposal and interview. (4) Because the tie-break puts the PROJECT PROPOSAL first, the two-page document is the highest-leverage artefact per hour of effort in the entire application. (5) Nobody in either 2026/27 list scored above 58/60, so a strong but imperfect application is fully competitive; the median admitted EU Early Bird score was 50.
bonus_points: NO BONUS POINTS EXIST. The 60-point scale is closed: 20 portfolio + 20 project proposal + 20 interview, with nothing added on top for any credential, achievement or circumstance. EXPLICITLY ABSENT, in contrast with other unibz programmes: NO Webometrics university-ranking bonus (Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science award 3 / 2 / 1 points for a bachelor from a top-1000 / 1001–2000 / 2001–3000 university) — a degree from a prestigious university earns an Eco-Social Design applicant nothing; NO GMAT or GRE bonus (Master in Accounting and Finance); NO C1 language bonus (EMMA awards 3 points for a C1 certificate, and that bonus decided its 2026/27 non-EU cut-off) — here a C1 or C2 certificate is worth exactly the same as a bare B2; NO cum laude bonus (EMMA awards 2 points); NO startup-project presentation bonus (Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation, 30 points); NO video-presentation or professional-CV points (Master in Energy Engineering). THE CV IS REQUIRED BUT NOT SCORED. 'curriculum vitae in English (pdf)' is a mandatory upload, yet it carries no line in the rubric. It functions as context for the commission's holistic judgement — 'the commission will decide, after judging the attitude and experience, which applicants will be admitted to the second stage' — and as material for the interview, where 'Experience in the field of the study programme' and 'Inter- and transdisciplinary experiences' are discussion topics. So professional experience can influence the interview score indirectly, but it can never add a point of its own. WHAT THIS MEANS IN PRACTICE: there is no way to buy or accumulate an advantage before applying. Every point must be earned inside the three assessed artefacts. For a candidate with a weak academic record this is the most forgiving admission at unibz; for a candidate with a strong academic record and a thin portfolio it is the least forgiving.
portfolio_and_materials:
THE PORTFOLIO AND THE PROJECT PROPOSAL ARE THE ADMISSION. Together they carry 40 of the 60 points and they alone decide who reaches the interview. unibz publishes unusually explicit assessment criteria for both — they should be treated as a marking rubric. 

PORTFOLIO — 20 POINTS. Format, verbatim: 'portfolio in English (pdf) max file size 20 MB. Please submit a fully illustrated and written portfolio as a PDF only. You can, of course, add links to external websites; however, ensure that this is for audio-visual material or material that the commission cannot otherwise consult via a PDF document. Note that the commission reserves the right to decline a portfolio that is not readily accessible to them.' That last sentence is a hard warning: a portfolio built as a link farm to Behance, Notion or a personal site can be REFUSED outright. Links are permitted only for audio-visual work that cannot live in a PDF. This tightened since 2022/23, when unibz accepted a 'conversion of a web-based portfolio (e.g. Behance) in PDF format indicating the URL'. Content, verbatim: 'It can contain also non-design projects in relevant fields (activism, social work, culture, volunteering, etc.)' — an explicit invitation to career-changers and non-designers. Criteria, verbatim: 'The works in the portfolio should show: the ecological and social relevance and potential transformation; Innovative and creative thinking; Formal design qualities (aesthetics, functionality, details); Framing and quality of the (visual) storytelling.' Note that only ONE of the four criteria is about craft; three are about relevance, originality and narration. A beautifully rendered but socially empty portfolio scores badly here. 

OUTLINE OF A PROJECT PROPOSAL — 20 POINTS, AND THE FIRST TIE-BREAK. Format, verbatim: 'outline of a project proposal (pdf), on which you would want to work for a semester. In max. two A4 pages, the main points must be explained and visualized concisely and appealingly. You may include text, images, graphics, etc. The required language is English.' Criteria, verbatim: 'The project outline should describe and contain: Ecological and social relevance and potential transformation; Creative thinking (we appreciate unconventional ideas and approaches); Framing and quality of the visual storytelling (we want to understand quickly the essentials, and still get an idea of the profound thinking behind); Tangible project idea(s) (we do not expect perfect solutions, but concrete proposals).' Three things are worth extracting from that wording. First, the proposal must be VISUALIZED, not merely written — 'explained and visualized'. Second, unibz states its own reading behaviour: 'we want to understand quickly the essentials' — the commission skims first. Third, it lowers the bar on completeness while raising it on concreteness: 'we do not expect perfect solutions, but concrete proposals'. The proposal describes work the applicant would actually do for a semester, which aligns with the programme's structure (semester 2 is 'an autonomous project ... together with external partners you choose'). Because the tie-break ranks proposal above interview above portfolio, two candidates on identical totals are separated by this two-page document. 

CURRICULUM VITAE — REQUIRED, NOT SCORED: 'curriculum vitae in English (pdf)'. No page limit, no template. 

ACADEMIC BACKGROUND — REQUIRED, NOT SCORED: see required_documents for the exact contents unibz demands. 

WHAT IS NOT REQUIRED: no motivation letter, no letters of reference, no research proposal, no video, no Excel study-career template (unlike EMMA and the engineering masters), no writing sample, and no physical portfolio. 

FORMAT LIMITS IN ONE LINE: portfolio = PDF only, max 20 MB, English; project proposal = PDF, max 2 A4 pages, English; CV = PDF, English. No word counts or character limits are published for any of them. 

HARD PROCEDURAL RULES: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' 'The Admission Committee will only evaluate the documents uploaded in the portal by the application deadline.' 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.' 

EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS WHERE APPLICATIONS DIE: in the 2026/27 non-EU Early Bird round, 14 of 24 documented applicants failed the 20/40 stage-1 gate, four of them scoring 4/40 and three scoring 2–3/40 — scores that low indicate submissions that ignored the published criteria rather than weak designers.
interview: YES — A COMPULSORY ONLINE INTERVIEW WORTH 20 OF 60 POINTS, ONE THIRD OF THE TOTAL, WITH PUBLISHED DATES. DATES 2026/27, verbatim from the admission-information PDF: EARLY BIRD — 'Interview (online): 14/05/2026'; LATE APPLICATION — 'Interview (online): 15/07/2026'. Both are single fixed dates, published months in advance, and both are ONLINE — no travel to Bolzano is required, which matters for overseas candidates. WHO IS INVITED: only applicants who clear the stage-1 gate. 'In order to be eligible for the second stage, you must have obtained at least 20 points' out of the 40 available for portfolio plus project proposal. 'Based on the documents received, the commission will decide, after judging the attitude and experience, which applicants will be admitted to the second stage of the admission process.' In 2026/27, 7 EU Early Bird applicants, 14 non-EU Early Bird applicants and 5 EU Late applicants were filtered out at this gate and never interviewed. WHAT IT IS, verbatim: 'The second stage consists in an online interview designed to have a dialogue to get a deeper understanding on the candidate's ideas, experiences, motivations and points of view.' The signed ranking list phrases it slightly differently: 'an interview designed to assess the experience gained'. PUBLISHED AGENDA, verbatim: 'In the interview we will discuss: Experience in the field of the study programme: Inter- and transdisciplinary experiences; Innovative and creative thinking; Ability to work in a team; Ability to discuss and to reflect critically.' Note the last two: teamwork and critical reflection are explicitly assessed, which fits a programme built on group studio projects with external partners. WHY IT MATTERS ARITHMETICALLY: a candidate who scrapes through stage 1 with the minimum 20/40 still needs 10 of 20 interview points to reach the 30/60 pass mark, and in 2026/27 an EU Early Bird applicant needed 44/60 overall to be admitted — so a weak interview is unrecoverable. Conversely the interview is the one place where a career-changer whose portfolio is thin on formal design craft can demonstrate the transdisciplinary experience the programme says it wants. TIE-BREAK POSITION: the interview score is the SECOND tie-break criterion, after the project proposal and before the portfolio. [uncertain] unibz does not publish the interview's duration, its format (panel or single interviewer), the composition of the commission, the platform used, whether candidates present their portfolio or proposal during it, or whether any accommodation is made for time zones. Non-EU applicants in distant time zones should raise this with design-art@unibz.it after applying. STABILITY: the interview, its 20-point weight and its agenda are identical in the archived 2022/23 admission PDF. The only change is that it is now explicitly labelled 'online' and given a fixed published date, where earlier cycles announced the interview together with the ranking-list publication window.
conditional_admission: YES — conditional admission is available and, unusually, imposes NO minimum-credit condition. THE RULE, verbatim from the admission-information PDF: 'If you have not yet graduated at the time of application: You can apply, but you will be admitted conditionally and need to submit your diploma by the enrolment deadline. If you graduate after the enrolment deadline: You cannot enrol and you will lose your place, which will be offered to the subsequent applicant in the ranking list. In this case you should not pay the tuition fees to secure your admission. You will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there still are available places, you can enrol by 11 December 2026.' The signed ranking list adds the exact deadline and the escalation path: 'Applicants who have not concluded their bachelor’s degree are provisionally admitted: requirement for admission is the conclusion of the bachelor studies by the enrolment deadline (13 October 2026, 12 midday). Advice: If you achieve your qualification after the enrolment deadline, you should not pay the tuition fees to confirm the study place. You will be able to submit a late enrolment request to the Rector and, only if there are study places still available, you can enrol by 11 December 2026.' GENEROUS ASPECT — NO CREDIT THRESHOLD. Unlike several unibz masters (≥120 ECTS already earned, or ≥140 for the Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management), Eco-Social Design imposes no floor on credits earned so far. Any enrolled bachelor student may apply. And because the score contains no grade component at all, a not-yet-graduated applicant suffers no scoring disadvantage either — there is not even a 'weighted average' substitute to compute, unlike EMMA. TIE-BREAK ASPECT — ALSO NEUTRAL. The tie-break order is project proposal, then interview, then portfolio, then youngest candidate. There is NO 'already graduated takes precedence' rule of the kind EMMA applies. Not having graduated is therefore costless in this programme, and the youngest-candidate rule at the very end mildly favours younger, typically not-yet-graduated applicants. WHAT TO UPLOAD IF STILL STUDYING: 'if not graduated yet: please upload the list of your passed exams'. HOW COMMON IT IS IN PRACTICE — the 2026/27 lists asterisk provisional admits, so this is measurable. Early Bird EU: four of the fifteen admitted were flagged as not yet graduated (IDs 155902 at rank 1, 153934 at rank 7, 154774 at rank 12, 155928 at rank 14) — including the highest-scoring applicant in the entire round. Late EU: one applicant flagged as not yet graduated (156951 at rank 9) plus six flagged with a double asterisk for a different reason. A SECOND, SEPARATE RESERVATION applies to foreign qualifications: 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified', and 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded. During enrolment, unibz verifies your foreign qualification and may request additional documents if necessary. If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' In the 2026/27 Late list SIX of the ten admitted carried this flag (157861, 157789, 157523, 140507, 146479, 157865) — i.e. the Late round was dominated by international applicants whose diplomas were still being verified. A THIRD applies to every non-EU citizen living abroad: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.' FINAL WARNING, verbatim: 'If you have been admitted in the ranking list, but you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector’s decree even after enrolment.'
ofa_rules: NOT APPLICABLE. OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) is an Italian instrument confined to FIRST-CYCLE programmes, where an applicant who fails a compulsory entrance test is admitted with a credit debt to be cleared during the first year. At unibz it is used in the Bachelor in Economics and Management, the Bachelor in Economics, Politics and Ethics and the Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management, all tied to a mathematics test. Eco-Social Design is a restricted-access SECOND-CYCLE programme with no entrance test, so the instrument cannot apply. Neither the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, nor the brochure, nor either signed 2026/27 ranking list mentions OFA, additional learning requirements, remedial obligations, credit debts or integration courses; the ranking lists carry no OFA markers. ITALIAN LAW DOES NOT ALLOW master-level admission with curricular credit debts settled after enrolment: the entry qualification (an Italian L-4 / L-17 / L-21 degree, or 10 ECTS in the listed design sectors, or a committee-approved foreign career) must be satisfied BEFORE admission, and the diploma must exist by 13 October 2026. THE FUNCTIONAL EQUIVALENT OF A REMEDIAL ROUTE therefore sits entirely on the pre-admission side, and — unlike EMMA, which explicitly points applicants to unibz single-subject enrolment — the Eco-Social Design documents do NOT name any remedy. [uncertain] A candidate who is short of the 10 design-sector credits would in principle be able to close the gap through unibz's single-subject-courses route (https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/single-subject-courses/) or through equivalent courses elsewhere and re-apply in a later cycle, but this programme's documents neither mention nor endorse that path; it should be confirmed with design-art@unibz.it. THE ONE THING THAT DOES CARRY OVER between sessions is the invitation to re-apply after exclusion: 'If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one', and the ranking-list note 'They may re-apply in the second session' — which three 2026/27 applicants used to convert an Early Bird exclusion into a Late admission or waiting-list place.
language_requirements:
ONE REQUIREMENT AND ONE ONLY: ENGLISH AT B2 (CEFR) TO GAIN ADMISSION. Verbatim from the admission-information PDF: 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.' There is NO German requirement, NO Italian requirement, NO third-language B1 threshold, and no exit level stated in the 2026/27 documents (see exit_levels for an important historical caveat). This is the lightest language profile available at unibz. 

THE GATE IS A HARD KNOCK-OUT AND IS THE MOST LETHAL FILTER IN THIS PROGRAMME'S ADMISSION. Failure to prove B2 removes you before your portfolio is scored, regardless of how good it is. In the signed 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list, NINE EU/parity applicants were listed under: 'The following persons do not meet the language requirements for admission and are therefore excluded from the admission procedure. They may re-apply in the second session.' — IDs 150498, 149844, 140507, 145298, 153713, 154365, 155633, 155035, 156074. Against roughly 40 documented EU applicants competing for 15 places, that is about 22% lost on paperwork. By comparison EMMA lost about 5% the same way. The non-EU list confirms the same mechanism: applicants outside the ranking 'were excluded from the admission procedure because they did not meet the admission requirements (language and/or study title)'. IT IS RECOVERABLE: ID 140507, language-excluded in Early Bird, was admitted at rank 5 in the Late round. 

WHERE AND HOW TO PROVE IT: in the Application Portal, under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', and — critically — those sections 'become available after you have created an application in the section create/manage applications'. So the sequence is: create the application first, then handle the language evidence. ADMINISTRATIVE FORM, verbatim: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.' FALLBACK DELIVERY, verbatim: 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.' 

B2 IS ENOUGH, AND MORE IS WORTH NOTHING IN POINTS. Unlike EMMA, this programme awards no bonus for a C1 certificate — see bonus_points. There is therefore no scoring reason to over-invest in a higher band; the only reason to hold C1 evidence is that the medium-of-instruction routes (high school or degree taught in English) are recognised AS C1 and are the cheapest and most robust proof available. 

NO SECOND OR THIRD LANGUAGE IS ASSESSED AT ANY POINT, in admission or in graduation. The admission PDF still carries the generic unibz line 'For information on studying in three languages also visit the following page', which is boilerplate for the trilingual programmes and does not create any obligation here. unibz Language Centre courses in German and Italian remain available on a voluntary basis and are genuinely useful for local project work and life in South Tyrol.
entry_levels_by_position: ENGLISH B2 in first position / NO second language / NO third language — in unibz's positional notation, B2 / none / none. unibz expresses language requirements by POSITION (1st, 2nd, 3rd teaching language) rather than by named language, because its trilingual programmes rotate which language sits in which slot. Eco-Social Design has only ONE teaching language, English, in first position, required at B2. No level is required in a second or third language at any stage of the two years. PLACING THIS ACROSS UNIBZ: trilingual bachelors run B2/B2/none (Bachelor in Computer Science) or B2/B1/none (Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering); trilingual economics masters run C1/B2/none (Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance, Master in Accounting and Finance); the sister Bachelor in Design and Art in the same faculty is trilingual and therefore effectively closed to English-only applicants. Against all of those, Eco-Social Design's single B2-in-English entry level is the least demanding language profile at unibz, tied with the other fully English-taught masters such as EMMA, Energy Engineering and Software Engineering. ONE PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC NUANCE: because every course, the thesis and the defence are in English on a single Italian campus, there is no second-country or second-language exposure of the kind EMMA creates by sending students to Innsbruck for year 2. The positional grid B2/none/none describes the lived reality of the degree accurately, not just its paperwork. THE ONLY LANGUAGE ELEMENT INSIDE THE DEGREE is a compulsory 3 CP course 'English 1 – Language Course' in the study plan, taught by the unibz Language Centre — an English-progression component, not a second-language requirement.
exit_levels: NO EXIT / GRADUATION LANGUAGE LEVEL IS STATED IN THE 2026/27 DOCUMENTS — but this is the single field where the current documentation is genuinely unreliable, and an applicant should verify it before relying on it. WHAT THE CURRENT DOCUMENTS SAY: the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, the 2026/27 brochure and both signed 2026/27 ranking lists contain only an entry level. The language section is headed 'Entry level (to gain admission)' and stops there. No exit level, no graduation language condition, no C1 requirement appears anywhere. [uncertain] WHAT THE ARCHIVED DOCUMENT SAYS: the 2022/23 admission-information PDF for the SAME programme stated, verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English and the following language requirements apply: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2. Exit level (to graduate) English: C1.' An explicit C1-to-graduate requirement therefore existed as recently as 2022/23 and has since vanished from the published text. unibz publishes no note explaining whether the requirement was ABOLISHED or merely OMITTED from the redesigned PDF template. This is the most consequential open question in this record: a C1 exit requirement, if still in force, is a graduation condition, not an admission one, and students in unibz's trilingual programmes routinely discover such conditions late. A RELEVANT PIECE OF EVIDENCE POINTING BOTH WAYS: the current study plan still contains a compulsory 3 CP course 'English 1 – Language Course'. Its existence suggests unibz still expects measurable English progression during the degree — the course would be the natural vehicle for reaching C1 — but passing a 3 CP course is not the same as certifying a CEFR level, and the course carries no published CEFR target. THE STRUCTURAL BACKGROUND: unibz operates two models. Trilingual programmes require, per the unibz Study Guide, two languages at C1 and the third at B1 in order to graduate. Fully English-taught programmes generally 'do not include language requirements in other languages'. Eco-Social Design sits firmly in the second group as far as GERMAN and ITALIAN are concerned — there is certainly no German or Italian exit obligation. The open question is only about English itself. WHAT TO DO: an admitted student should ask design-art@unibz.it and the unibz Language Centre, in writing, whether a C1 English exit level applies to the LM-12 cohort they are joining, and get the answer before the end of the first semester. If it does apply, the cheapest routes are the same medium-of-instruction recognitions used at entry (an English-medium high school final year or an English-medium degree are both recognised AS C1), which most international students in this programme already hold.
third_language_exam_threshold: NOT APPLICABLE — there is no second and no third teaching language, therefore no third-language B1 threshold and no language-based gate on sitting exams. The rule this field is designed to capture — a B1 level in the third language required from the second semester of the first year in order to be allowed to sit examinations — belongs exclusively to unibz's TRILINGUAL programmes, such as the Bachelor in Computer Science or the sister Bachelor in Design and Art. It appears nowhere in the Eco-Social Design 2026/27 admission-information PDF, brochure or signed ranking lists, and it cannot apply to a programme whose 'official teaching language is English' full stop and whose entire published course offering is tagged EN. There is likewise no first-language exam threshold gating exam attendance: once admitted with B2 English, no further language certification is required in order to sit any examination in the programme. The only language condition attached to Eco-Social Design is the B2 English entry gate, settled before admission. The one language-related obligation INSIDE the degree is passing the compulsory 3 CP course 'English 1 – Language Course', which is an ordinary examination worth credits, not a CEFR threshold. The generic sentence 'For information on studying in three languages also visit the following page', which unibz prints in every programme's admission PDF, is template boilerplate and creates no obligation here.
proof_pathways:
FOUR ACCEPTED WAYS TO PROVE ENGLISH B2, listed verbatim in the admission-information PDF as 'You can demonstrate language proficiency through:'. Two of them require no test at all, and for most international applicants one of those two is the correct answer. 

PATHWAY 1 — MEDIUM OF INSTRUCTION AT HIGH SCHOOL, RECOGNISED AS C1: 'the main teaching language in your final high school year, if English (recognised as C1). Foreign qualifications: If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.' 

PATHWAY 2 — A DEGREE TAUGHT IN ENGLISH, RECOGNISED AS C1: 'a bachelor or master degree in English (recognised as C1). unibz graduates must upload the language certificates obtained and/or declare that they have passed language exams at the unibz Language Centre (B2, B2+ or C1). Foreign qualifications: If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies.' THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SENTENCE IN THE WHOLE LANGUAGE SECTION for an international design applicant. It is free, instant, and recognised at C1 rather than B2. The clause 'If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction' is precisely where the nine 2026/27 Early Bird exclusions most plausibly originated: a diploma that does not itself say 'medium of instruction: English' is not enough, and the supplementary registrar's letter must be uploaded WITH the application, not sent later. 

PATHWAY 3 — A RECOGNISED CERTIFICATE: 'a recognised language certificate (see the list of recognised certificates). If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.' The governing list is unibz's 'Recognised language certificates and diplomas – Students and applicants (Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026)' at https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf — see certificate_rules. 

PATHWAY 4 — A UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE EXAM, ONLINE: 'language exams organised by the unibz Language Centre. You can register for these exams online through the application portal (in the section “enrol for language exams”) after you have filled out your application in the section “create/manage applications”.' 2026/27 SITTINGS AND REGISTRATION WINDOWS, verbatim: EARLY BIRD — '16/03/2026 (registration: 02 - 09/03/2026) and 16 - 17 and 20 - 21/04/2026 (registration: 24/03 - 08/04/2026)'; LATE — '22 - 26/06/2026 (registration: 28/05 - 15/06/2026)'. THE TRAP, verbatim: 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' Registering for the exam is a separate action from submitting the application, it lives inside the portal, and it is only visible after an application exists. An applicant who submits on the last day of the Early Bird window (28/04/2026) has already missed both Early Bird exam registration deadlines (09/03 and 08/04) and both sittings — which is a mechanically guaranteed language exclusion. 

ORDER OF OPERATIONS THAT AVOIDS THE PROBLEM: (1) create the application in the portal on day one of the window; (2) immediately check whether pathway 1 or 2 applies and, if so, request the registrar's medium-of-instruction letter at once; (3) if neither applies, register for a Language Centre exam inside the current registration window, or obtain a recognised certificate before the application deadline; (4) only then spend the remaining weeks on the portfolio and project proposal. 

DEADLINE FOR EVERYTHING LANGUAGE-RELATED is the application deadline of the session concerned: 28/04/2026 for Early Bird and for all non-EU applicants, 02/07/2026 for the EU Late session.
certificate_rules:
GOVERNED BY UNIBZ'S UNIVERSITY-WIDE RULES, NOT BY THE PROGRAMME: 'Recognised language certificates and diplomas – Students and applicants (Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026)', published trilingually at https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf. Only English matters for this programme. 

GENERAL CONDITIONS, verbatim from the English section of that document: 'In order to be recognised, an international certificate or any proof of language proficiency must meet the following requirements: 1. include the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself; 2. indicate adequate performance in all skills in the form of an overall grade (and/or the detailed assessment is indicated on the certificate itself or by appropriate documentation faithful to the original by the certification organisation).' THE LOWEST-SUBSKILL RULE, verbatim: 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the examination has been passed. There is no compensation for “failed” parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation.' A candidate with strong reading and weak speaking is graded on the weak one. FIVE-YEAR VALIDITY, verbatim: 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January.' Certificates listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' — which is where the medium-of-instruction routes sit — 'will have unlimited validity'. That is another reason to prefer pathway 1 or 2: they never expire. WHAT IS REFUSED, verbatim: 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam (“home edition”) are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list. Certificates regarding single skills issued by different certification organisations will not be accepted. Certificates of participation, certificates of end-of-course-tests and examinations from private educational institutions as well as results of placement tests will not be recognised. Certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff will not be recognised. DAAD certificates are not recognised.' 

ENGLISH SCORE BANDS FOR B2 (the level this programme needs) AND C1, from the English table: IELTS Academic or General — B2 = 5.5–6.5, C1 = 7.0–8.0, C2 = 8.5+ (B1 = 4.0–5.0). TOEFL iBT — B2 = 72–94, C1 = 95–113, C2 = 114–120 (B1 = 42–71). Pearson PTE Academic — A2 = 30–42, B1 = 43–58, B2 = 59–75, C1 = 76–84, C2 = 85–90. Cambridge English — B2 = 'B2 First (FCE): grade B, C', 'B2 Business Vantage (BEC Vantage): grade B, C', or 'C1 Advanced (CAE): level B2'; C1 = 'C1 Advanced (CAE)', 'B2 First (FCE): grade A', 'C1 Business Higher (BEC Higher): grade B, C', or 'C2 Proficiency (CPE): level C1'. Trinity College London ISE — B2 = 'ISE II (B2)', C1 = 'ISE III (C1)'. University of Michigan — B2 = 'MET – B2 (all 4 skills)' or ECCE; C1 = 'MET – C1 (all 4 skills)'; C2 = ECPE. LanguageCert, Pearson PEIC, Gatehouse Awards Classic IESOL and GATE, English Speaking Board and the Oxford Test of English are also listed at their nominal levels. TOEIC is accepted with per-skill minima (B2 = 'Listening 400+; Reading 385+; Speaking 160+; Writing 150+'; C1 = 'Listening 490+; Reading 455+; Speaking 180+; Writing 180+'). HOME EDITION: the asterisked entries — which include IELTS, TOEFL, TOEIC, LanguageCert and several others — carry the footnote '* Also accepted as “home edition”'. Cambridge, Trinity and Michigan entries are not asterisked. DUOLINGO ENGLISH TEST DOES NOT APPEAR ANYWHERE IN THE LIST and must be assumed not recognised. [uncertain] The IELTS and TOEFL rows in the source PDF are laid out across five CEFR columns and the extracted text places the values slightly out of order; the mapping above is reconstructed from the internally consistent TOEFL, PTE and Cambridge rows and matches unibz's published practice, but a candidate at a band boundary (for example IELTS 5.5 or TOEFL 72) should have the Language Centre confirm it in writing rather than rely on this reconstruction. NOTE ON WHAT THE PROGRAMME ADDS: nothing. Eco-Social Design imposes no programme-specific certificate rule, no minimum sub-score of its own, and no bonus for exceeding B2.
application_deadline_eu:
TWO SESSIONS ONLY FOR EU AND PARITY-OF-TREATMENT APPLICANTS IN 2026/27 — there is NO Additional Application Session for this programme (see below), which distinguishes it from most other unibz masters. 

SESSION 1 — EARLY BIRD APPLICATION, verbatim: 'Application: 02/03 - 28/04/2026 (by noon local time)'. ISO: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, 12:00 local (CEST) on the closing day. Open to EU citizens, citizens given parity of treatment, AND non-EU citizens living abroad. 

SESSION 2 — LATE APPLICATION, verbatim: 'Late Application (only for EU citizens) — Application: 28/05 - 02/07/2026 (by noon local time)'. ISO: 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-02, 12:00 local. Restricted to EU citizens and those treated as equivalent; non-EU applicants living abroad are barred. 

NO ADDITIONAL SESSION. unibz ran an Additional Application Session for 2026/27 'from 18 August to 4 September' with studies commencing in October 2026, but the Master in Eco-Social Design is NOT among the programmes included. Of the Faculty of Design and Art's masters, only the Master in Critical Creative Practices reopened in that round. So for 2026/27 an EU applicant had exactly two chances, both now closed. 

RE-APPLYING BETWEEN SESSIONS IS EXPLICITLY PERMITTED AND DEMONSTRABLY WORKS, verbatim: 'You might apply for more than one study programme. If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one.' The ranking lists repeat 'They may re-apply in the second session' next to both the language exclusions and the stage-1 failures. In 2026/27 three applicant IDs did exactly this and improved sharply — see selection_scoring. 

THE LATE SESSION WAS THE BETTER BET IN 2026/27. Early Bird offered 15 EU places and closed at a 44/60 cut-off; Late offered 10 EU places and closed at 32/60. Late also inherits unfilled Early Bird places: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.' A borderline EU candidate with time to strengthen the portfolio should seriously consider the Late window rather than rushing Early Bird. 

HISTORICAL COMPARISON, showing the windows are stable to within days: 2022/23 ran Early Bird 01/03–28/04/2022 and Late 19/05–07/07/2022. A 2027/28 applicant should plan for an Early Bird window opening in the first days of March 2027 and closing at the end of April 2027, and a Late window from late May to early July 2027 — but must confirm on the 2027/28 admission PDF once published (typically from around December–February). 

ALL DEADLINES ARE AT NOON, NOT MIDNIGHT. unibz writes '(by noon local time)' on every single application deadline. This catches applicants out every year.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE WINDOW ONLY, AND IT IS THE EARLY BIRD WINDOW. Verbatim: 'Non-EU-Citizens (living outside of Italy) — Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' THE WINDOW for 2026/27 was the Early Bird one: 'Application: 02/03 - 28/04/2026 (by noon local time)' — ISO 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, 12:00 local (CEST). The Late Application session is labelled 'only for EU citizens' and is closed to non-EU applicants living abroad, and the Additional Application Session does not include this programme at all. A non-EU applicant living abroad therefore has exactly ONE chance per academic year, with no second session and no recovery — in sharp contrast to EU applicants, for whom a failed Early Bird can be converted into a Late admission. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LANGUAGE GATE: because there is no second session, a non-EU applicant who mishandles the English evidence loses the entire year. The language-exam sittings available to them are only the Early Bird ones — 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026) and 16–17 and 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026) — so the language question must be resolved in the first weeks of March, not in late April. WHO COUNTS AS NON-EU LIVING ABROAD: everyone who is not an EU citizen and does not hold one of the qualifying Italian residence permits — see parity_of_treatment. Crucially: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' AFTER ADMISSION, verbatim: 'Once the ranking list has been published, if you have gained admission, secure it by paying the first instalment and then start your visa application on the Universitaly portal. The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' SO THE NON-EU 2026/27 CHAIN IS: apply by 28/04/2026 noon → interview 14/05/2026 → ranking list by 27/05/2026 (published signed on 18/05/2026) → pay the € 600 first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon → Universitaly pre-enrolment → consulate visa → enrol by 13/10/2026 noon → residence permit within 8 working days of arrival. COMPETITION IN 2026/27: 10 places advertised, only 9 admitted (the 10th place was left empty rather than admit an applicant on 28/60), with admitted scores of 55, 52, 51, 48, 42, 41, 37, 37, 32 and fourteen further applicants eliminated at the 20/40 stage-1 gate. Non-EU applicants therefore faced a much weaker field than EU Early Bird applicants (whose cut-off was 44) — the binding constraint for non-EU candidates is meeting the 30/60 absolute threshold, not out-competing the field. HISTORICAL: the same single-window rule applied in 2022/23, when the fee was € 30 and 9 non-EU places were offered.
parity_of_treatment:
THE THIRD CATEGORY, AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST TO A TURKISH READER WHO IS ALREADY IN ITALY OR EUROPE. unibz splits applicants into EU citizens, citizens 'given parity of treatment' (who follow the EU route in every respect), and non-EU citizens living abroad. VERBATIM, from the admission-information PDF: 'Considered as equivalent are: 1. Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; 2. Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: “permesso di soggiorno” (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay. A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid. If the permit has expired, you must attach a renewal request. Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' 

THE FOUR QUALIFYING PERMIT TYPES ARE: work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, and religious reasons. A STUDENT permit does NOT qualify — stated explicitly — and neither does a tourist visa. This is the most commonly misunderstood point in the whole unibz application system: a Turkish student already studying in Italy on a study permit is still treated as a non-EU citizen living abroad. 

WHY PARITY IS WORTH A GREAT DEAL IN THIS PROGRAMME SPECIFICALLY, quantified from the 2026/27 results: (1) TWO SESSIONS INSTEAD OF ONE — parity applicants may use both Early Bird and the Late Application, and the Late session's cut-off was 32/60 against Early Bird's 44/60. A candidate scoring in the mid-30s was rejected in Early Bird and would have been comfortably admitted in Late. Non-EU applicants living abroad get no such second chance. (2) A SECOND CHANCE AFTER EXCLUSION — 'If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one', which three 2026/27 applicants used successfully. (3) NO € 50 APPLICATION FEE — the fee applies only to non-EU applicants living abroad. (4) NO UNIVERSITALY PRE-ENROLMENT, NO CONSULATE STEP, NO VISA, NO PROOF OF € 24,000 IN MEANS, and no dependence on 'the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz' — all admitted non-EU applicants living abroad are only provisionally admitted until that communication arrives. (5) A ROUTE TO PROVINCIAL SCHOLARSHIPS — non-EU students can only apply for a South Tyrol study grant with a long-term residence permit or after 'their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption'; someone already resident in Italy on a work or family permit is far closer to that threshold. 

TOTAL EU/PARITY PLACES IN 2026/27: 25 (15 Early Bird + 10 Late) against 10 for non-EU applicants living abroad. 

WHAT TO UPLOAD: a copy of the valid permesso di soggiorno, or the renewal request if it has expired — inside the application portal, before the deadline. Omitting it silently reclassifies the applicant into the harder, single-window, fee-paying, visa-dependent track.
places_quotas:
THREE SEPARATE QUOTAS, TOTALLING 35 PLACES. Admission-information PDF, verbatim: 'Available places — EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: Early Bird Application: 15; Late Application: 10. Non-EU citizens (living abroad): Early Bird Application: 10.' The brochure 'At a glance' summarises the same thing as 'Places available: 25 EU + 10 non-EU'. 

HOW THE QUOTAS ACTUALLY FILLED IN 2026/27: EU EARLY BIRD — 15 places, 15 admitted, quota FULL, plus a 9-person waiting list (ranks 16–24, scores 44 down to 31). Cut-off 44/60, with the same score 44 appearing at both rank 15 (admitted) and rank 16 (waitlisted), so the last place turned on the tie-break. EU LATE — 10 places, 10 admitted, quota FULL, plus a 3-person waiting list all on 30. Cut-off 32/60. NON-EU EARLY BIRD — 10 places, only NINE admitted. The quota did NOT fill: one applicant scored 28/60 and was excluded because 'The following applicant did not reach the required minimum score of 30/60 and is therefore excluded from the ranking.' unibz left a funded place empty rather than lower the standard. Lowest admitted non-EU score: 32. TOTAL ADMITTED FOR 2026/27: 34 against 35 places. 

QUOTA CARRY-OVER, verbatim: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.' So the EU Late round can exceed its nominal 10 if Early Bird admits fail to pay. Note the asymmetry: unfilled NON-EU places do not carry over to anyone. 

WAITING LISTS ARE REAL AND HAVE PUBLISHED ACTIVATION DATES: 'Applicants from rank 16 are on the waiting list and will only be able to join the programme if the admitted people do not secure their admission by the deadline. Those on the waiting list will be contacted by e-mail as of 8 June 2026 in case a spot opens up' (Early Bird), and the equivalent Late clause names 7 August 2026. 

DOCUMENTED APPLICANT PRESSURE (a lower bound, since applicants excluded on qualification grounds are not listed at all): EU Early Bird — 15 admitted, 9 waitlisted, 7 failed the stage-1 gate, 9 excluded on language = 40 documented for 15 places. EU Late — 10 admitted, 3 waitlisted, 1 below the pass mark, 5 failed the gate = 19 documented for 10 places. Non-EU Early Bird — 9 admitted, 1 below the pass mark, 14 failed the gate = 24 documented for 10 places. Overall roughly 83 documented applicants for 35 places, i.e. a documented selectivity of about 41%. That is competitive but far from brutal by international design-master standards, and the biggest single cause of failure is a weak stage-1 submission, not an oversubscribed quota. 

HISTORICAL TREND: 2022/23 offered 17 EU Early Bird + 8 EU Late + 9 non-EU = 34 places, under a rule that the programme 'will only be offered if a minimum of 12 newly enrolled students is reached'. By 2026/27 the split had shifted to 15 + 10 + 10 = 35 and the minimum-enrolment clause had been dropped. The direction of travel is a slightly larger, slightly more international, more Late-weighted intake. [uncertain] 2027/28 quotas are not yet published; unibz has adjusted this split at least once in the last four cycles, so the 15/10/10 figures should be re-checked against the 2027/28 admission PDF.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates:
EARLY BIRD 2026/27 — PUBLISHED DEADLINES, verbatim: 'Interview (online): 14/05/2026'; 'Publication of ranking lists: by 27/05/2026'; 'Payment of the 1st instalment of the tuition fees: by 05/06/2026 (by noon local time)'; 'Enrolment: from 10/07 - 13/10/2026 (by noon local time)'. Signed by the President, Prof. Christian Krois. The first instalment of tuition fees amounts to € 600.00'; 'from 10 July until 13 October 2026, 12 (midday), enrol online in the Application portal'. WAITING LIST ACTIVATION: 'Those on the waiting list will be contacted by e-mail as of 8 June 2026 in case a spot opens up' — i.e. three days after the payment deadline. 

LATE APPLICATION 2026/27, verbatim: 'Interview (online): 15/07/2026'; 'Publication of ranking lists: by 23/07/2026'; 'Payment of the 1st instalment of the tuition fees: by 06/08/2026 (by noon local time)'; 'Enrolment: from publication of the ranking list until 13/10/2026 (by noon local time)'.
