Waiting-list activation: 'Those on the waiting list will be contacted by e-mail as of 7 August 2026 in case a spot opens up'. 

ISO NORMALISATION (unibz writes DD/MM/YYYY): interviews 2026-05-14 and 2026-07-15; rankings by 2026-05-27 (actual 2026-05-18) and by 2026-07-23 (actual 2026-07-16); first-instalment deadlines 2026-06-05 12:00 and 2026-08-06 12:00; enrolment window 2026-07-10 to 2026-10-13 12:00 for Early Bird, publication-to-2026-10-13 12:00 for Late; graduation deadline for provisional admits 2026-10-13 12:00; late enrolment to 2026-12-11. 

THE PAYMENT DEADLINE IS THE REAL DEADLINE, not the enrolment one. 'If you do not meet this deadline, you will automatically be excluded and the next applicant in the ranking list will be admitted.' Paying € 600 by 05/06 (Early Bird) or 06/08 (Late) is what reserves the place; enrolling later merely completes it. AND PAYING IS NOT ENROLLING, verbatim: 'Please note: Paying university fees does not confer student status, which is only obtained by enrolling. If you pay but do not enrol, you are not entitled to a refund, except for non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the necessary documents for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country.' HOLDING TWO OFFERS: 'If you have been admitted to more than one study programme, you can secure your admission for a maximum of 2 programmes by paying the designated rate twice. By confirming your place, you renounce admission to the other programmes.' ENROL EARLY, verbatim: 'Enrolment is recommended as early as possible, so you have the possibility to upload incomplete documents before the deadline.' LATE ENROLMENT SAFETY VALVE: a Rector-approved late enrolment request, 'only if there are study places still available', up to 11 December 2026. TRANSFERS: 'Students intending to transfer from another Italian University to unibz must submit to the Student Office - at the beginning of the academic year - a copy of the transfer application presented at the university of provenance.' RANKING LISTS EXPIRE: 'The ranking lists with the admitted students will be published here: https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/ranking-lists/ and are only valid for the respective academic year.' unibz removes prior-year lists — probing the 2025 Ranking-Lists paths returns 404 — so 2026/27 competition data should be archived by anyone who needs it.
programme_specific_dates:
THE PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC DATE THAT DOES NOT EXIST FOR MOST UNIBZ MASTERS IS THE INTERVIEW, AND IT IS FIXED AND PUBLISHED: 'Interview (online): 14/05/2026' for Early Bird and 'Interview (online): 15/07/2026' for Late Application. Single dates, online, announced in the admission PDF months ahead. Every admitted student in 2026/27 was interviewed on one of those two days. 

LANGUAGE EXAM DATES (programme-listed, Language Centre-run, online): Early Bird — '16/03/2026 (registration: 02 - 09/03/2026) and 16 - 17 and 20 - 21/04/2026 (registration: 24/03 - 08/04/2026)'; Late — '22 - 26/06/2026 (registration: 28/05 - 15/06/2026)'. Note this programme's Late block offers only the June sitting, with no July date, because its Late application closes 02/07/2026. 

FULL 2026/27 ACADEMIC CALENDAR AS PUBLISHED FOR THIS PROGRAMME, verbatim: 'Freshers Days: 28 - 29/09/2026'. 1st semester: 'Classes: 28/09 - 23/12/2026'; 'Holidays: 24/12/2026 - 06/01/2027'; 'Classes: 07 - 23/01/2027'; 'Exams: 25/01 - 20/02/2027'. 2nd semester: 'Classes: 01/03 - 25/03/2027'; 'Holidays: 26 - 29/03/2027'; 'Classes: 30/03 - 12/06/2027'; 'Exams: 14/06 - 10/07/2027'. Autumn session: 'Exams: 23/08 - 25/09/2027'. Note that teaching starts on the SAME DAY the Freshers Days end (28/09/2026 appears in both lines) — there is no settling-in week. 

CONSEQUENCE FOR NON-EU ADMITS: the enrolment deadline (13/10/2026) falls AFTER classes have already begun (28/09/2026), so a student whose visa is slow will miss the opening weeks of a programme whose first semester is built around a collaborative studio project. Given that semester 1 is explicitly designed 'to create a shared basis for team/group work' and 'to facilitate your landing in unibz and the environs of Bozen-Bolzano', arriving late has a real cost here that it would not have in a lecture-based degree. Non-EU admits should start the Universitaly and consulate process the moment the first instalment is paid in June. 

WORKSHOP SEQUENCING, a programme-specific timing rule with no published date but a fixed order: mandatory safety training (Work Safety – Machinery Hazard – Chemical Risk) → introductory workshop courses in semester 1 → 'From the second semester onwards, you must choose and attend at least one specialised workshop.' 

FREE CHOICE COURSES: 'At the beginning of each academic year, the Faculty announces which courses are offered and recognised as free choice' — an annual, undated announcement students must watch for. 

NO OTHER PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC DATES EXIST: no portfolio submission date separate from the application deadline, no test date, no on-campus assessment day, no mandatory pre-course, and no separate thesis-registration deadline published in the admission documents. Everything creative is due at the application deadline itself — 28/04/2026 noon or 02/07/2026 noon.
required_documents:
FIVE THINGS, AND NOTABLY NO EXCEL TEMPLATE. Verbatim, 'The following documents need to be uploaded in the application portal', plus the ID required at account creation. 

(0) ID AT ACCOUNT CREATION: 'You need to create an account and upload a valid ID card or passport (front/back). Please note: if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' 

(1) ACADEMIC BACKGROUND, verbatim and in full because the required contents are unusually specific: 'if graduated in Italy: diploma supplement or substitute-declaration (following the Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000) of the degree awarded, final grade, exams passed with corresponding grade, the dates in which the exams were passed, the credit points, the subject areas, and the teaching hours; if graduated abroad: diploma supplement or final degree certificate issued by the foreign university (to be translated into English if in a language other than Italian, German or English) detailing the final mark, exams passed as well as corresponding grades, the dates in which the exams were passed, the credit points, and the teaching hours. A description of the contents of single courses is recommended; it is advisable to attach a declaration of value or similar document by the university with the indication of the lowest grade needed in order to achieve the degree as well as the highest mark obtainable; if not graduated yet: please upload the list of your passed exams.' TWO ITEMS FOREIGN APPLICANTS ROUTINELY OMIT AND SHOULD NOT: TEACHING HOURS per exam (needed for the committee to judge the 10-ECTS design-sector equivalence) and the DECLARATION OF VALUE stating the lowest passing grade and the highest obtainable grade. For a Turkish transcript that means supplying the registrar's grading-scale page (e.g. minimum 2.00 to graduate on a 4.00 maximum) rather than a self-written note, plus course descriptions/syllabi in English. 

(2) 'curriculum vitae in English (pdf)'. 

(3) 'outline of a project proposal (pdf) ... In max. two A4 pages ... The required language is English'. See portfolio_and_materials. 

(4) 'portfolio in English (pdf) max file size 20 MB ... as a PDF only'. See portfolio_and_materials. 

(5) IF THE QUALIFICATION WAS GAINED ABROAD, ALSO THE DIPLOMA: 'If you gained your qualification abroad, you must also upload the diploma of your qualification: if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you’ll need to upload it upon enrolment.' 

(6) FOR PARITY-OF-TREATMENT APPLICANTS: a copy of the valid Italian permesso di soggiorno, or the renewal request if expired. Omitting it reclassifies the applicant as non-EU living abroad. 

(7) LANGUAGE EVIDENCE, which is technically handled in its own portal section rather than the document list: a recognised certificate, or a medium-of-instruction letter, or registration for a Language Centre exam. This is the item that eliminated nine EU applicants in the 2026/27 Early Bird round. 

WHAT IS NOT REQUIRED, and is required by comparable unibz masters: NO structured study-career Excel template (EMMA, Energy Engineering and Software Engineering all demand one and reject applications without it); NO motivation letter; NO reference letters; NO video; NO research proposal; NO GMAT/GRE report. The Eco-Social Design upload set is short but creatively demanding. 

AT ENROLMENT, FOR A FOREIGN DEGREE, THREE FURTHER DOCUMENTS: 'degree diploma of your Bachelor'; 'official translation of your degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English)'; 'Diploma supplement, where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme' — plus the ARDI/CIMEA statements described in credential_recognition. 

HARD RULES: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified.' 'Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' 'The Admission Committee will only evaluate the documents uploaded in the portal by the application deadline.' 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.'
application_fee: € 50, PAID ONLY BY NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING OUTSIDE ITALY. Verbatim, under 'Non-EU-Citizens (living outside of Italy)': 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment pay NOTHING to apply — no fee appears anywhere in their section of the admission-information PDF. This is one more reason to upload a qualifying permesso di soggiorno if you hold one. The fee is not described as refundable anywhere in the 2026/27 documents, and unibz's general rule is that it is not returned. It is separate from and additional to the € 600 first tuition instalment that secures an admitted place, and separate from the € 16 revenue stamp embedded in that instalment. [uncertain] The documents do not state whether the € 50 is charged per application or per applicant; since non-EU applicants have only one session and, on Universitaly, 'can apply for one study programme only', the distinction has little practical effect for this programme. HISTORICAL: the archived 2022/23 admission PDF for the same programme set the fee at € 30 — it has risen by two thirds in four cycles, so a 2027/28 applicant should budget for € 50 or slightly more and check the current PDF. IN CONTEXT, the € 50 is trivial beside the real costs a non-EU applicant faces: CIMEA Statement of Comparability and Statement of Verification fees, sworn translations if the diploma is not in Italian, German or English, an English certificate if the medium-of-instruction route does not apply, the € 600 first instalment payable before any visa is granted, and proof of at least € 24,000 in available means for the two-year master.
tuition_or_fees_link:
APPROXIMATELY € 1,200 PER YEAR — among the cheapest design masters in Western Europe, and the same flat figure unibz charges across almost all its programmes. Brochure 'At a glance': 'Tuition fees: ca. € 1200 per year'. Admission-information PDF, verbatim: 'Fees amount to € 1200. 1st instalment (€ 600): includes the revenue stamp of € 16. 2nd instalment (€ 600): must be paid by March of the following year.' The signed ranking list confirms the first instalment is what secures the place: 'The first instalment of tuition fees amounts to € 600.00', payable 'within 5 June 2026, 12 (midday)' for Early Bird admits and by 06/08/2026 for Late admits. FULL RULES: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees 

DETAIL FROM THE CENTRAL FEES PAGE FOR 2026/27: students within the normal course duration plus one year pay € 600 by 13 October 2026 and € 600 by 31 March 2027. From the SECOND year beyond the normal duration the first instalment rises to € 900 (a € 300 surcharge) with the second instalment remaining € 600 — so a student who takes more than three years over this two-year master pays € 1,500 in that year. Late payment of the second instalment 'will result in a fine (30 Euro) being levied', and the account is blocked: 'If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes.' Students who graduate by 31 October avoid the new year's fees; those graduating by 31 March pay only the € 16 stamp duty. 

NO REFUNDS: 'If you drop out of a programme, interrupt your studies or are excluded from studies, you are not entitled to reimbursement of the fees.' The only exception is a non-EU applicant living abroad who pays the first instalment and then fails to obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities. 

EXEMPTIONS, verbatim: 'Exemption from the tuition fees is granted to: Students with a disability recognized under article 3, paragraph 1, of Law No 104/1992, or with a disability up to or exceeding 66%: the disability certificate, issued by the health authorities, must be handed in at the beginning of the academic year. Foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government.' Exempt students still pay the € 16 revenue stamp. 

REFUND VIA PROVINCIAL SCHOLARSHIP: 'Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees.' 

[uncertain] MATERIALS COSTS ARE NOT PUBLISHED AND ARE NOT TRIVIAL FOR THIS PROGRAMME. Eco-Social Design is a workshop-intensive design master — wood, metal, plastic, plaster and mould making, screen and tampon printing, bookbinding, photography, video, Fab Lab BITZ — and unibz publishes no figure for consumables, prototyping materials, printing, model-making or software. Applicants should budget separately for these; the € 1,200 covers tuition only. 

TOTAL DIRECT TUITION for the two-year degree at the standard rate: about € 2,400, against living costs of at least € 800 per month that the visa authorities require non-EU students to evidence.
scholarships_grants:
THE HEADLINE FACT FOR A NON-EU APPLICANT: THE MAIN SCHOLARSHIP IS EFFECTIVELY UNREACHABLE IN THE FIRST YEAR. The principal financial aid at unibz is the ordinary study grant of the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol, administered by the provincial Office for Higher Education Support (Amt für Hochschulförderung), not by unibz. The eligibility bar for non-EU citizens is stated bluntly, verbatim: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption.' A newly arrived Turkish student on a first-year study permit satisfies neither condition, and unibz's own non-EU applicant page repeats that provincial scholarships become available only after 'one year of regular registered residence in South Tyrol'. In practice this means: fund year 1 yourself, and apply for the grant for year 2. [uncertain] The provincial grant is commonly cited in the region at roughly € 1,680–€ 6,960 per academic year depending on income, family situation and whether the student lives away from home; that band could NOT be verified from a live unibz or provincial page during this research (the unibz study-grants page links out rather than publishing figures, and the direct scholarship URL returned 404). The amount, the income thresholds and the 2026/27 deadlines must be checked against the provincial Office for Higher Education Support before being relied on. unibz directs applicants to that office, to study@unibz.it, and to the South Tyrolean Students Association (asus.sh) for help with the application. 

WHAT IS DOCUMENTED AND CERTAIN: (1) A provincial scholarship also brings a TUITION REFUND — 'Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees.' (2) A FULL TUITION EXEMPTION (€ 16 stamp only) exists for 'Foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government' — i.e. the MAECI/Invest Your Talent in Italy route, which a Turkish applicant can pursue independently of unibz and which is not subject to the South Tyrol residence rule. This is the single most realistic funding route for a first-year non-EU student in this programme. (3) A FULL TUITION EXEMPTION also exists for students with a disability recognised under Law 104/1992 or with disability of 66% or more. (4) unibz separately offers merit scholarships and 'grants for fostering postgraduate studies' through the same provincial framework, plus accommodation support; details are held by the Office for Higher Education Support. 

NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC SCHOLARSHIP. Neither the 2026/27 admission-information PDF nor the brochure nor the programme page names any Eco-Social Design or Faculty of Design and Art scholarship, bursary, fee waiver or studio grant. There is no design-specific funding attached to this master, and — unlike some unibz programmes — no industry-sponsored places. 

OTHER ROUTES WORTH KNOWING: Erasmus+ mobility grants for the exchange semesters the programme offers; project funding, which the programme itself teaches as a skill through the seminar 'Project Funding for Eco-Social Designers'; and part-time work, which a non-EU study permit allows at 'no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year'. 

BUDGET REALITY: € 1,200 tuition plus at least € 800 per month living costs means roughly € 10,800–€ 12,000 for a first year that will almost certainly be unfunded for a non-EU student, and the visa itself requires evidence of at least € 24,000 for the two-year master.
credential_recognition:
TWO SEPARATE PROCESSES, AT TWO DIFFERENT MOMENTS — do not confuse them. 

AT APPLICATION: no ARDI or CIMEA document is required. The Selection Committee assesses the foreign career itself: 'If you have a degree from the Italian old system (prior to D.M. 509/99), or a title from another degree, or a degree obtained abroad, the selection committee will examine your career to determine your eligibility for admission.' What must be uploaded is the diploma supplement or final degree certificate with grades, dates, credit points and TEACHING HOURS, translated into English if not already in Italian, German or English, with course content descriptions 'recommended' and a declaration of value 'advisable'. 

AT ENROLMENT: the formal recognition machinery kicks in, and it is country-dependent. Verbatim: 'If you have a foreign university degree, during enrolment you must upload: degree diploma of your Bachelor; official translation of your degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English); Diploma supplement, where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme.' Then, 'Depending on the foreign education system your degree belongs to, you must also upload: a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein: Statement of Correspondence of your Bachelor degree, to be downloaded from the ARDI - Automatic Recognition Database – Italy. b) Non-EU countries that are signatories to the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Correspondence of your Bachelor degree, to be downloaded from the ARDI - Automatic Recognition Database – Italy and Statement of Verification of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA). c) Non-EU countries that are not signatories of the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Comparability of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA) and Statement of Verification of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA).' 

WHICH BOX DOES TURKEY FALL INTO? Türkiye is a party to the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so a Turkish applicant falls under CATEGORY (b): an ARDI Statement of Correspondence PLUS a CIMEA Statement of Verification. That is the cheaper and faster of the two non-EU routes — category (c) applicants must buy a full CIMEA Statement of Comparability as well. [uncertain] unibz does not publish its own country list; applicants should confirm their country's category with the Student Office before paying CIMEA fees, since ARDI coverage is built country by country and a specific Turkish institution may not yet be represented in the database. 

TRANSLATION: an Italian translation of the degree is required unless the documents were issued in German or English. A Turkish university that issues an English diploma and English transcript therefore avoids the sworn-translation cost entirely — worth requesting from the registrar in advance. Note the asymmetry with the application stage, where ENGLISH translation suffices; at enrolment the requirement is ITALIAN. 

THE ADMISSION IS PROVISIONAL UNTIL THIS IS DONE, verbatim: 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified'; 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded. During enrolment, unibz verifies your foreign qualification and may request additional documents if necessary. If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' In the 2026/27 Late ranking list, SIX of the ten admitted EU applicants carried this flag — it is the normal state of an international admit, not a warning sign. AND THE RESERVATION SURVIVES ENROLMENT: 'Please note that if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector’s decree even after enrolment.' 

GENERAL UNIBZ PROCEDURE: https://www.unibz.it/en/services/recognition-foreign-qualifications/general-procedure/ 

TIMING ADVICE: CIMEA statements routinely take weeks. An Early Bird admit learns the outcome around 18–27 May and must enrol by 13 October — that is enough time only if the CIMEA request is filed immediately after the ranking list appears, and ideally started before it.
non_eu_visa_process:
A SIX-STEP CHAIN, EVERY LINK OF WHICH CAN BREAK THE ADMISSION. 

STEP 1 — APPLY IN THE SINGLE WINDOW: 02/03–28/04/2026, noon. 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' No Late session, no Additional session for this programme. 

STEP 2 — SECURE THE PLACE BEFORE ANY VISA EXISTS: 'Once the ranking list has been published, if you have gained admission, secure it by paying the first instalment and then start your visa application on the Universitaly portal.' The € 600 first instalment was due by 05/06/2026 noon. This is money paid months before a visa decision — the one refund unibz allows is precisely for this case: a refund is available for 'non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the necessary documents for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country'. 

STEP 3 — UNIVERSITALY PRE-ENROLMENT, MANDATORY AND SINGLE-CHOICE: 'The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' The ranking list is harsher: 'Non-EU citizen living abroad will also have to apply on the Universitaly portal of the Italian Ministry of Universities and Research. In Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only. Should you not follow this procedure, your direct online application to unibz will be declared null and void.' Portal: https://www.universitaly.it/ 

STEP 4 — THE CONSULATE, WHICH UNIBZ CANNOT CONTROL: 'Please note that preliminary admission by unibz does not guarantee obtaining a visa, the issuing of which is the exclusive responsibility of embassies and consulates. Likewise, obtaining a visa for study purposes does not confer any right to perfecting the enrolment in a study programme.' unibz's non-EU page adds that admission does 'not guarantee an appointment at the diplomatic-consular Italian representation'. And the admission is conditional on the consulate reporting back: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.' PROOF OF FINANCIAL MEANS required for the visa, from unibz's non-EU applicant page: a minimum of € 800 PER MONTH in the Bozen-Bolzano area covering 'accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing', and total available means of 'at least € 24,000' for a MASTER programme (the bachelor figure is 'at least € 36,000'), plus health insurance and visa expenses on top. For this programme the € 24,000 figure applies. 

STEP 5 — ENROL BY 13/10/2026, 12:00, uploading the diploma, the Italian translation if needed, the Diploma Supplement showing ≥180 ECTS and master access, and the ARDI/CIMEA statements. Note that classes start 28/09/2026, so a visa delay means missing the opening of a studio-based semester built on team formation. Late enrolment via a Rector's request runs to 11/12/2026 'only if there are study places still available'. 

STEP 6 — RESIDENCE PERMIT WITHIN 8 WORKING DAYS OF ARRIVAL: 'According to Italian law, within 8 working days of your arrival in Italy, you must have applied for the residence permit: as soon as you arrive, get in touch with the Advisory Service and you will be given the necessary information for starting the procedure. Once you will obtain your residence permit (permesso di soggiorno), you have to hand it in at the Student Office personally or via e-mail.' 

WORKING WHILE STUDYING: a study residence permit allows part-time work 'for no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year'. 

SCHOLARSHIPS ARE OUT OF REACH IN YEAR 1: provincial study grants require a long-term residence permit or 'one year of regular registered residence in South Tyrol'. 

A CATEGORY TRAP WORTH REPEATING: a study permit never converts you into a parity-of-treatment applicant, and 'if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad'. Conversely, a Turkish citizen already holding an Italian work, family, asylum or religious permit should upload it and skip this entire chain. 

REFERENCE: https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/international/international-degree-seeking-applicants/degree-seeking-non-eu-citizens-living-abroad/

DATA VINTAGE: everything here reflects the 2026/27 admission cycle, from documents stamped 'Latest update: 15.07.2026' and from two signed ranking lists protocolled 18/05/2026 and 16/07/2026. Verified on 2026-08-29. The 2026/27 cycle is CLOSED — both application windows have expired, both ranking lists are published, and this programme is not in the Additional Application Session. A new applicant is targeting 2027/28, for which NO dates, NO quotas and NO documents exist yet. Everything time-sensitive below must be re-verified against the 2027/28 admission-information PDF when unibz publishes it (historically around December–February). 

1. EXIT LANGUAGE LEVEL — THE MOST IMPORTANT OPEN QUESTION. The 2026/27 documents state no exit level. The archived 2022/23 admission PDF for the same programme stated 'Exit level (to graduate) English: C1'. unibz publishes nothing explaining whether the requirement was abolished or simply dropped from a redesigned template. The study plan still contains a compulsory 3 CP 'English 1 – Language Course', which cuts both ways. An admitted student must confirm this in writing with design-art@unibz.it and the Language Centre. 

2. SCHOLARSHIP AMOUNTS UNVERIFIED. The provincial study grant is widely cited at roughly € 1,680–€ 6,960 per year, but that range could not be confirmed from a live unibz or provincial page during this research (unibz's study-grants page links out without figures; a direct scholarships URL returned 404). Treat the band as indicative only. The residence condition for non-EU students is confirmed and is the decisive fact. 

3. THE SSD LIST IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT. Eight codes are pre-2024 (ICAR/13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 21; L-ART/06; ING-INF/05) and one is post-2024 ('INF-01 Informatics'). unibz publishes no crosswalk to the new CEAR-xx/x and informatics codes for this programme. Applicants with new-format Italian transcripts should get written confirmation of the correspondence. 

4. THE ACCADEMIE DI BELLE ARTI / ISIA ROUTE VANISHED FROM THE PRINTED LIST. Named explicitly in 2022/23 (DAPL03, DAPL04, DAPL05, DAPL06, DAPL08, DIPL01, DIPL02), absent in 2026/27. Such candidates most likely still qualify via the committee catch-all, but this is inference, not a published rule. 

5. DEGREE-CLASS TYPOS IN THE OFFICIAL DOCUMENTS. The admission PDF's double-enrolment clause cites 'LM-69/LM-69' and the signed ranking list cites 'LM-18/LM-18'; the correct example for this programme is LM-12/LM-12. Neither document ever prints it correctly. 

6. THE NON-EU RANKING LIST IS NOT IN SCORE ORDER. Rank 3 carries 48 and rank 4 carries 51 in the signed Early Bird list. One of the two columns contains an error that unibz does not annotate. 

7. FOUNDING YEAR. The 2015/16 start is sourced from the programme's own blog ('10 years of Eco-Social Design') and third-party listings; unibz publishes no founding date in any official document. 

8. INTERVIEW MECHANICS UNPUBLISHED. Duration, format (panel or single interviewer), commission composition, platform, whether the portfolio is presented live, and time-zone accommodation for overseas candidates are all unstated. 

9. GRADE STATISTICS LACK A REFERENCE PERIOD. The LM-12 exam and graduation distributions carry no stated cohort range or sample size; the graduation percentages imply roughly 52 graduates, but unibz does not say over how many years. 

10. WHAT CHANGED IN THE 2025 STUDY-PLAN REVISION IS NOT PUBLISHED. unibz maintains separate 'enrolled after 2025' and 'enrolled before 2025' course offerings without a changelog. 

11. FACULTY REGULATIONS NOT READ. The LM-12 regolamento didattico on records-unibz.siavcloud.com refused automated retrieval (HTTP 403). Binding academic rules — including any graduation language condition, attendance obligations and thesis regulations — live there and were not inspected. 

12. IELTS/TOEFL BAND MAPPING RECONSTRUCTED. The certificate PDF's five-column table extracts out of order; the B2/C1 bands cited here are reconstructed from the internally consistent TOEFL, PTE and Cambridge rows. A candidate at a boundary (IELTS 5.5, TOEFL 72) should get written confirmation. Duolingo does not appear in the list at all and must be assumed unrecognised. 

13. MATERIALS AND WORKSHOP COSTS UNPUBLISHED. A workshop-intensive design master with no published figure for consumables, prototyping, printing or software. The € 1,200 covers tuition only. 

14. NUMBERS EXCLUDED BEFORE THE RANKING ARE UNKNOWN. Both lists end with 'Applicants not included in the ranking list were excluded from the admission procedure because they did not meet the admission requirements', without counts. The ~83 documented applicants for 2026/27 are therefore a LOWER BOUND on the true applicant pool. 

15. RANKING LISTS ARE EPHEMERAL. Prior-year files return 404 and 'are only valid for the respective academic year'. The 2026/27 competition data captured here will disappear from unibz's servers. 

16. NO CONFLICTS FOUND BETWEEN THE PROGRAMME PAGE, THE BROCHURE AND THE ADMISSION PDF. Unusually for unibz, the HTML page reproduces the admission PDF verbatim and the brochure is a strict superset of it. Where this record cites a figure, all available sources agreed. The only cross-source discrepancies are the two degree-class typos and the non-EU rank/score ordering, both noted above. 

17. NO COMMUNITY OR APPLICANT-EXPERIENCE SOURCES FOUND. Searches across Reddit and general forums for first-hand accounts of this programme's portfolio, proposal or interview returned nothing usable; the only substantive non-unibz sources are aggregator listings (Mastersportal, educations.com) which merely restate the official text, and the programme's own blog. All admission findings in this record therefore rest on unibz primary documents.
